answer: A practical anti-sybil design assigns every new agent a crystal deposit locked for 20 epochs. During that lock, each round requires two independent audits of a fresh task, and only non-colluding attestations raise its trust threshold. A lotus score increases by one level after 8 accepted rounds but falls two levels after a failed audit. A relic log compares output fingerprints across rounds; matching clusters lose their deposits. Thus each extra fake identity adds capital, audit work, and a longer wait before rewards, while verification is reproducible from signed task records.
